items.title: Understanding Statistical Statements
items.explanation: A statistical statement is a claim or summary about a phenomenon expressed using numerical values, such as predictions or trends. For example, 'I expect a century from Jemimah in tomorrow's match' is a statistical prediction based on her consistent batting. Similarly, 'The population of their village has reduced by about 100 in the last decade' is a summary statement derived from collected data.

items.title: Identifying Statistical Questions
items.explanation: A statistical question can be answered by collecting and analyzing data. Examples include 'How tall are Grade 7 students in our school?' or 'Approximately how many bricks are in this wall?'. In contrast, questions like 'What is the price of a tennis ball in India?' (which requires current market data) or 'Who was the best bowler yesterday?' (which refers to past specific events) are not statistical questions because they do not involve collecting new data for prediction.

items.title: Calculating Average Runs
items.explanation: To determine who performed better, we calculate the average number of runs scored per match. For Shubman: 110 runs ÷ 5 matches = 22 runs per match. For Yashasvi: 96 runs ÷ 4 matches = 24 runs per match. Since 24 > 22, Yashasvi performed better on average.
